flagged.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheets. Where clearances are required to be dimensioned, the dimension lines must extend from the outside conductor (not from utility pole centerline or pole structure). On multi-conductor installations, the outermost conductor may be several feet offset from pole center.

flagged.comment: Dimension lines and clearance annotations on submitted plans show distances from property lines, easement boundaries, and pole locations, but do not originate from the outside conductor location. Per UCM § 1.10.3 and the measurement methodology in the regulatory overview, all clearances must be measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), not from utility pole centerline or easement boundaries. On multi-conductor installations, the outermost conductor may be several feet offset from pole center. Dimension lines must explicitly show origin at conductor position.
areas: All overhead electric clearance areas

flagged.comment: Plans show overhead lines but provide no clearance dimension callouts measuring distances from features to overhead conductors. The specific species of these mitigation trees are not identified on the landscape plan, making it impossible to verify whether they are utility-compatible species per ECM Appendix F. Trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors must be from the Utility Compatible list. Provide plant schedule identifying each mitigation tree species and verify compliance with utility-compatible requirements.
areas: Trees planted near overhead electric line on southern property boundary

Without confirmed species identification for the trees near the overhead line, utility-compatible status cannot be verified against ECM Appendix F. This is mandatory separate requirement from permanent clearances. Plans must include logistics plan or note addressing construction phase clearances from overhead lines.
